title: Odd Positions First
statement:
Number the nodes of a linked list `1, 2, 3, ...` from the head. Rearrange the list so that **all nodes at odd positions come first, then all nodes at even positions**, keeping the original order inside each group. Return the head.

Do it by re-linking the existing nodes, using only a constant amount of extra memory.

examples.explanation: Odd positions: 2, 3, 6, 7. Even positions: 1, 5, 4. The values themselves do not matter, only the positions.

hints.nudge: Build two chains at once while you walk along the list: one for the odd positions and one for the even positions. When you are done, how do the two chains join?
hints.pattern: Two pointers re-linking the list in place: odd.next skips over one node, even.next skips over one node; finally the odd chain's tail points to the head of the even chain.
hints.pseudocode:
if the list is empty: return empty
odd = head; even_head = even = head.next
while even and even.next:
  odd.next = even.next; odd = odd.next
  even.next = odd.next; even = even.next
odd.next = even_head
return head
hints.walkthrough: Remember where the even chain starts (the second node). Keep a pointer on the last odd node and a pointer on the last even node. In each round, the odd chain takes the node after the current even node (odd.next = even.next, then move odd), and the even chain takes the node after that (even.next = odd.next, then move even). Stop when the even pointer or its next is missing: then the odd chain has taken every odd-position node. Finally link the end of the odd chain to the start of the even chain. Make sure the last even node's next ends up empty: the loop's own updates handle that. No nodes are copied, so memory is O(1) and every node is touched once: O(n).
